sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A perennial herb of meadows, pastures, slopes and grassland, including mountain sites. Stems are usually 30–120 cm tall.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The linear leaves grow in whorls of 6–12. Dense panicles bear fragrant yellow flowers 2–3.5 mm across; the smooth dry fruits turn black when ripe and split into two parts.

sections.title: Use
sections.text: The flowers have traditionally been used to help curdle milk in some cheeses. This does not recommend eating the whole plant.
